question: The Barakar is a tributary of river:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Damodar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Barakar River is the largest tributary of the Damodar River.
 
• It originates in the Hazaribagh plateau in Jharkhand, India.
 
• The Barakar River merges with the Damodar River near Dishergarh in West Bengal.
 
• The river flows through the states of Jharkhand and West Bengal before joining the Damodar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Damodar River**

 
 
• The Damodar River is known as the "Sorrow of Bengal" due to its frequent flooding in the past.
 
• It flows through the Indian states of Jharkhand and West Bengal.
 
• The river is approximately 592 kilometers (368 miles) long.
 
• Several dams and reservoirs have been constructed on the Damodar River for flood control and hydroelectric power generation, including the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) projects.
 
 
 
• **Tributaries of Damodar River**
 
 
• Besides Barakar, other significant tributaries include the Konar, Bokaro, and Haharo rivers.
 
• These tributaries contribute to the Damodar River's flow and play a role in the region's hydrology.
 
 
 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC)**
 
 
• Established in 1948, the DVC is a government-owned organization responsible for the management of the Damodar River basin.
 
• It focuses on flood control, irrigation, water supply, and electricity generation in the Damodar Valley region.
 
 
 
• **Hazaribagh Plateau**
 
 
• It is a part of the Chota Nagpur Plateau located in the state of Jharkhand.
 
• The plateau is rich in minerals, including coal, mica, and bauxite.
 
• The Barakar River originates from this plateau, contributing to its geographical significance.
